case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread concerns Bluetooth SIG registration support for an existing product that is being updated to use a replacement BLE module after the original module reached end-of-life. The discussion covers registration strategy, Bluetooth SIG fee handling, preparation of compliance-folder documentation, review of the new Bluetooth SIG registration system, and final completion of the registration process. Questions are raised about product-list management, registration review pages, TCW handling, and member-profile data visibility. The engagement concludes with registration completion, compliance-folder delivery, and invoicing.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: A key qualification topic is whether replacing an EOL BLE module in an existing product requires a new Bluetooth SIG registration; the conclusion is that a new registration is required. The thread explains that a new registration must contain at least one product model in the Product List, while additional models can be added afterward through the Product List maintenance process. The consultant also explains how Review Pages relate to publicly visible registration data, clarifies the role of TCWs in resolving Bluetooth SIG inter-layer dependency issues, and notes that member-company profile fields are automatically sourced from the SIG membership database rather than the registration workflow. Compliance-folder preparation requirements are also defined, including user documentation, block diagrams, product drawings, and antenna documentation.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's reasoning is based on Bluetooth SIG registration rules rather than product branding. Even though the commercial product name remains unchanged, replacing the BLE module creates a qualification scenario that requires a new registration. Registration validity is determined by the qualified Bluetooth implementation and associated design references, not solely by the marketed product identity. The consultant also distinguishes between registration-managed information, member-database-managed information, and post-registration Product List maintenance activities.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Assuming that a BLE module replacement can be covered by an existing registration could result in use of an invalid qualification basis for the updated product. Misunderstanding Product List management could lead to incorrect product registration entries that later require Bluetooth SIG correction requests. Failure to prepare required compliance-folder documentation could delay project closure and qualification record completion. Confusion regarding TCWs or registration-review data could also slow the declaration and review process.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a Bluetooth product changes to a different BLE module, first determine qualification impact based on the Bluetooth implementation rather than the product name. For Bluetooth SIG registrations under the newer qualification system, separate qualification decisions into three categories: qualification scope, registration/declaration workflow, and member-account data management, and verify each independently before submission.
